corrections.source_says: Describe selected semantic area: selected text strings are embedded with Google Universal Sentence Encoder v4 into 512-dimensional vectors, reduced with UMAP using cosine similarity to a shared 2D space, and summarized by the area of each participant's convex hull. The hull uses SciPy quick hull and area uses the shoelace formula. This is within-person semantic breadth (flexibility), not across-person homogenization.
corrections.quote: For this we used Google’s Universal Sentence Encoder v4 (Cer et al. 2018), but any sufficiently rich embedding model could be used.

confirmed: Read the complete markdown conversion and all 9 PDF pages, including References; no appendix or supplement is identified (PDF pp. 1-9). The source version is accurately limited to the undated ICCC proceedings PDF on file; PDF metadata subject is Proceedings of ICCC. The document title and five listed authors match the form (p. 1).

A single DesignAID dataset reanalysis is reported, not a synthesis or a new independent experiment (PDF p. 3, Evaluating Creative Ideation with Semantic Area; p. 8, Cai et al. reference). The default synthesis counts and pooled-estimate fields are appropriate.

The design is described as a 2x2 factorial, all participants used Direct and Diverse modes, and Figure 6 explicitly calls the comparison within-subjects (PDF p. 3, Methods/Results; p. 5, Figure 6). Neither allocation nor randomized condition order is stated anywhere in the PDF. has_randomized_people_study=false here means no randomized people study is confirmed by this source, not proof of nonrandom allocation; retain design_class=other, criterion_1=unclear, core=unclear, and context_class=none pending original-design evidence.

The analyzed sample is 111 people from the original 115, restricted to at least 3 unique inputs; the original randomized count and separate per-mode analyzed counts are not given (PDF p. 3, Data preparation). This is not a fewer-than-50-person sample, so criterion_2=met is correct.

The separately reported 9106 text strings and 5058 unique strings are text units, not participant or evaluator counts (PDF p. 3, Data preparation). Do not substitute them for people or infer a count of independently analyzed moodboards or ratings.

Participants created two moodboards for a chair for children; both modes generated images, while Diverse additionally used LLM-expanded text. The generative model names are not supplied (PDF p. 3, Results). Creativity-relevant ratings are scored on the final artifacts, supporting criterion_3=met (p. 3, external evaluations).

S1-O1 reported and one_line_finding match the PDF: selected area t = −8.54, p < .0001, MDiff = −8.54, with Diverse areas greater than Direct areas (PDF p. 4, Semantic Area and Mode of Interaction). The identical t and MDiff numbers are printed in the source; no correction or recomputation is warranted.
S1-O2 reported matches the objective innovation indirect association: b = −.01, z = −2.33, p = .02 (PDF p. 6, Effects Between What People Do, What People See, and What People Select, Figure 8a).

S1-O3 reported matches the objective fit indirect association: b = −.01, z = −2.44, p = .02 (PDF p. 6, same section, Figure 8b). These are mediation results through Input-to-Selected centroid distance, as the form correctly states.

Table 1 separately reports no significant linear association between input, seen, or selected semantic area and any objective rating (PDF p. 5, Table 1 and Semantic Area and Evaluated Outcomes). The negative indirect mediation results should not be represented as those direct regressions or as treatment-arm effects.

Selected semantic area measures variation within a participant's selected ideas; the flexibility classification is appropriate, and this is not an across-people diversity measure (PDF pp. 2-3, Semantic Area and Calculating and Using Semantic Area).
summary: The PDF confirms 111 analyzed DesignAID users and all three reported numerical results, but it does not establish random assignment or randomized condition order. The form needs corrections for preregistration, shared-sample attribution, company involvement, exclusions, and incomplete outcome documentation; randomized-study status remains unconfirmed.
